question: The position vectors of the points $P$ and $Q$ are $2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ and $-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, respectively. Determine the ratio in which a point $R$ lying internally on $PQ$ must divide the line segment so that $\overrightarrow{OR}$ is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{PQ}$, and hence obtain the position vector of $R$.
explanation: Formation of the Position VectorLet $R$ divide $PQ$ internally in the ratio $\lambda:1$. If`\vec{p}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}`and`\vec{q}=-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+2\hat{k},`then the position vector of $R$ is`\vec{r}=\frac{\lambda\vec{q}+\vec{p}}{\lambda+1}`Therefore,`\vec{r}=\frac{(2-\lambda)\hat{i}+(1+3\lambda)\hat{j}+(-1+2\lambda)\hat{k}}{\lambda+1}`Applying the Perpendicularity ConditionThe vector from $P$ to $Q$ is`\overrightarrow{PQ}=\vec{q}-\vec{p}=-3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}`Since $\overrightarrow{OR}$ is perpendicular to $\overrightarrow{PQ}$,`\vec{r}\cdot\overrightarrow{PQ}=0`As $\lambda+1$ is nonzero, the numerator gives`-3(2-\lambda)+2(1+3\lambda)+3(-1+2\lambda)=0-6+3\lambda+2+6\lambda-3+6\lambda=015\lambda-7=0\lambda=\frac{7}{15}`Thus, the required ratio is`\lambda:1=7:15`Evaluation of the Position VectorUsing the ratio $7:15$,`\vec{r}=\frac{7\vec{q}+15\vec{p}}{22}\vec{r}=\frac{7(-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+15(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})}{22}\vec{r}=\frac{23\hat{i}+36\hat{j}-\hat{k}}{22}`Final ResultThe point $R$ divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $7:15$, and its position vector is $\frac{1}{22}(23\hat{i}+36\hat{j}-\hat{k})$.

options.A: $R$ divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $15:7$, and $\overrightarrow{OR}=\frac{1}{22}(23\hat{i}+36\hat{j}-\hat{k})$.
options.B: $R$ divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $7:15$, and $\overrightarrow{OR}=\frac{1}{22}(23\hat{i}-36\hat{j}-\hat{k})$.
options.C: $R$ divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $7:15$, and $\overrightarrow{OR}=\frac{1}{22}(23\hat{i}+36\hat{j}+\hat{k})$.
options.D: $R$ divides $PQ$ internally in the ratio $7:15$, and $\overrightarrow{OR}=\frac{1}{22}(23\hat{i}+36\hat{j}-\hat{k})$.
